# PR #1731: Patch: an unreadable game record is quarantined instead of wedging the statistics fold

Closes #1715

## What changed

The fold of pending game records no longer stops on a record it cannot read. Before this, one such record failed the whole batch on every pass and blocked every record queued behind it. Now each record is read on its own:

- A record whose detail does not parse is marked folded, counted in no total, and has its detail emptied (`folded = true, record = null`).
- Its id stays, so a second write of the same game is still refused and no later fold takes it again. `game_records_list` already filters on `record is not null`, so it skips the record and no longer fails once the fold has run.
- The rest of the batch folds.
- `game_records.fold_poison` is alerted with the record's id and the parse error, once per record, after its batch has committed. A batch that fails to commit is retried and alerts nothing first.
- `jackioh-server stats-fold` prints each record it set aside.

## How it is built

- `store.rs`: `Tx::game_records_fold_pending` now returns a new `FoldedRecords { folded, unreadable: Vec<UnreadableGameRecord> }`, where each unreadable record carries its id and message.
- `pg.rs`: it selects `id, record` and parses each row separately. Readable rows update as before; unreadable ones get `set folded = true, record = null` in a second update. This needs no migration, because 0041's checks already allow a folded row with no detail.
- `fake.rs`: a new `FakeTables.unreadable_game_records` map emulates such a row. The fake's fold copies Postgres, and its other behaviour is unchanged.
- `api/game_records.rs`: `fold_pending` alerts and returns `FoldedRecords`. The loop's "batch was full" test counts folded plus set-aside records, so a batch holding a poison row does not end the loop early.
- `api/retention.rs` and `cli/stats_fold.rs` follow the new return type.
- Spec: new ruling `R1715000`, the first number of issue #1715's block. It amends R1044000 and R1044001 (titles and `cards` updated). It also adds a closing paragraph in `11-rulings.md`, a sentence in §9.11 and one in `crates/server/README.md`, and regenerates `INDEX.md`. No catalog fragment is needed, because no card plays differently.

## Tests

- Contract case `r1715000_sets_an_unreadable_record_aside_and_folds_every_record_behind_it`, on both stores. It plants an unreadable record whose id sorts first, then checks:
  - A fold batch of 2 returns `folded: 1` plus the set-aside record, and the totals match the one record counted.
  - The next fold takes the remaining 5 records, the one after that finds nothing, and the totals equal those of all six records.
  - `game_records_list` returns exactly the six readable records.
  - Writing the unreadable id again is refused and changes no total.
- API test `r1715000_the_fold_alerts_once_on_each_record_it_sets_aside`: exactly one `alert`-level `game_records.fold_poison` naming the id and message, the ledger row folded, and no second alert on a second fold.

# #1715: Patch: an unreadable game record is quarantined instead of wedging the statistics fold
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The server periodically folds stored game records into the running card-statistics totals. The fold reads a batch, and if even one stored record cannot be parsed — an old row written before the current format, or drift between deploys — the entire batch is abandoned, and abandoned again on every later pass: the bad row sits at the head of the queue forever and nothing behind it is ever counted. The same unreadable row also makes the record-listing endpoint fail. After the change, the unreadable row is set aside with an alert naming it, the rest of the batch is counted, and statistics keep flowing.

## Why

`game_records_fold_pending` selects a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` batch ordered by id and parses every row before marking any folded; a single parse error aborts the transaction (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:4656-4687`). The head-of-line poison row is retried on every retention pass (`api/retention.rs` logs `game_records.fold_failed` and retries), blocking every record queued behind it. `game_records_list` parses identically, so the same row 500s that read (:4645-4650). Migration 0041's folded check keeps the poisoned row permanently — the purge only empties folded rows. Reachability: `game_records_insert` validates at write, so poison needs pre-0041 rows — exactly the rows this fold exists to consume — or schema drift across deploys.

## Proposal

Per-record isolation: catch the parse error per row, mark that row folded (or set a quarantine flag) with a `game_records.fold_poison` alert naming its id, and fold the rest of the batch. Skipping a row that can never parse is strictly better than letting it block all later rows.

## Where it lands

`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/store.rs` (trait), `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, `crates/server/src/api/retention.rs`; tests in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` (the harness already has a raw-SQL escape hatch, `StoreHarness::forget_game_record_folds`, for planting a bad JSONB row). Spec §9.11, R1044000.

## Acceptance criteria

- A planted malformed record does not stall the batch: every later row folds.
- The poisoned row is marked (never retried) and its id logged or alerted.
- `game_records_list` no longer fails on the quarantined row (or explicitly excludes it).
- Contract test covers the case; fake store keeps its current contract.

## Size and risks

Small-medium. Decide quarantine-vs-mark-folded: marking folded loses the record, but an unparsable one is uncountable either way — an alert keeps it visible. The pg-only path naturally lives in the Docker contract suite; the fake can no-op or emulate via a flag.

Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The server periodically folds stored game records into the running card-statistics totals. The fold reads a batch, and if even one stored record cannot be parsed — an old row written before the current format, or drift between deploys — the entire batch is abandoned, and abandoned again on every later pass: the bad row sits at the head of the queue forever and nothing behind it is ever counted. The same unreadable row also makes the record-listing endpoint fail. After the change, the unreadable row is set aside with an alert naming it, the rest of the batch is counted, and statistics keep flowing.

## Why

`game_records_fold_pending` selects a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` batch ordered by id and parses every row before marking any folded; a single parse error aborts the transaction (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:4656-4687`). The head-of-line poison row is retried on every retention pass (`api/retention.rs` logs `game_records.fold_failed` and retries), blocking every record queued behind it. `game_records_list` parses identically, so the same row 500s that read (:4645-4650). Migration 0041's folded check keeps the poisoned row permanently — the purge only empties folded rows. Reachability: `game_records_insert` validates at write, so poison needs pre-0041 rows — exactly the rows this fold exists to consume — or schema drift across deploys.

## Proposal

Per-record isolation: catch the parse error per row, mark that row folded (or set a quarantine flag) with a `game_records.fold_poison` alert naming its id, and fold the rest of the batch. Skipping a row that can never parse is strictly better than letting it block all later rows.

## Where it lands

`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/store.rs` (trait), `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, `crates/server/src/api/retention.rs`; tests in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` (the harness already has a raw-SQL escape hatch, `StoreHarness::forget_game_record_folds`, for planting a bad JSONB row). - A planted malformed record does not stall the batch: every later row folds.
- The poisoned row is marked (never retried) and its id logged or alerted.
- `game_records_list` no longer fails on the quarantined row (or explicitly excludes it).
- Contract test covers the case; fake store keeps its current contract.

## Size and risks

Small-medium. Decide quarantine-vs-mark-folded: marking folded loses the record, but an unparsable one is uncountable either way — an alert keeps it visible. The pg-only path naturally lives in the Docker contract suite; the fake can no-op or emulate via a flag.
